title: Returned Deposit Payments on the Home Purchase Agreement: Deposits Held and the Cure Period
content:
A deposit payment on a Home Purchase Agreement that the buyer's bank returns unpaid is treated as follows.

**1. Effect on deposits held.** A returned deposit payment comes off the deposits held.

**2. Retired fee clause.** The former clause under which a returned payment fee of the collection's returned-payment fee is charged is **no longer in force**; the returned-payment charge is figured under the current basis that superseded it.

**3. Cure period.** Replacement funds and the fee must post within the collection's returned-payment cure business days after the date Calloway was notified of the return. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Calloway holidays, and counting starts the next business day after the notification date. The notification date is the date on the returned-payment entry of the agreement ledger, and the replacement is tied to the returned payment by its receipt number.

**4. Method.** Replacement funds must come by wire.

**5. Uncured return.** An uncured return on a ratified agreement is a buyer default under the agreement's buyer default and termination terms; on an agreement still pending ratification it simply leaves the signing deposits unfunded.

| Agreement status when the return stays uncured past the cure period | Result |
|---|---|
| Ratified (including under construction or closing scheduled) | Buyer default under the default and termination terms |
| Pending ratification | The signing deposits are left unfunded |

*Boundary (hypothetical calendar).* Calloway is notified of a return on a Friday, with no Calloway holiday in the following week, in a collection whose cure figure is 3 business days. The counted business days are Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday; replacement funds and the fee posting by Wednesday are within the cure period, and posting first on Thursday is not.
